brief: Two loose ends on one subject: the river's SURFACE. (a) #145 put the town in the water and five casters re-run their own draw — bridge, deck, mill wheel, jetty, willow — and #163 added 18 reed runs. The BOATS are the class it left out, and they are the only things on the water that MOVE: two punts, the barge, the rowboat, a standing punter. A hull with no image is the one object the eye checks. (b) PREMISE NOT RE-MEASURED BY ME: the cue raised at #159 says #163's water shade is correct and barely reads — 6021 px of mass but only 1-86 px of change — and that what makes a shadow read on water is cutting the SHEEN (`drawRiverFlow`'s streaks and the glitter column) rather than deepening the multiply. Verify that on HEAD with a SAME-CODE control before building on it. Quote every mass as a ratio to that control floor, never as an absolute.
successLooksLike: A punt under way carries its own image and the image moves with it; the mirror's mass for the boats is a stated multiple of a same-code control's zero. On a bright afternoon the town's shade on the near river is legible in the wide shot, and the number that changed is the sheen's, not the multiply's.
avoid: NOT through the offscreen: #163 measured 18 clipped runs at 1.6 ms a frame in `rcv` against 0.03 for the identical 56 clumps on the visible canvas. A clip plus an alpha is a `save()` on `ctx`. The boats move every frame, so this is a LIVE pass, never the ground cache. Do not deepen the multiply — the cue's whole point is that it is the thing that does not work. `onChannel` must keep the fountain and the pond on the land path.
